ds_min < d (d-0.18..d-0.33), s_max > s_min, dc_max > 1.3*s_max and > 1.7*d, k1_min < k_max

s_max column follows 8,10,13,15,16,18,21,27: this is the DIN 6921 table itself (NOT the EN 1665 / flange-nut series 18,21,24,30) -- confirmed by 6 independent sources incl. one reseller (Lawson) listing M12 across flats 16
shape_hint: Hex-head bolt with an integral round flange (washer face) under the head: the head is a short hexagon (height k) sitting on a thin circular flange of diameter dc whose rim is a thin lip of thickness c; the flange underside is slightly conical/concave, the shank is a plain cylinder with a thread of length b at the tip and a fillet/transition at the head.

role_map.b: thread length for bolt lengths L<=125
role_map.c_min: minimum thickness of the flange edge
role_map.k1_min: minimum height of the wrenching hex portion

notes: DIN 6921 (original 1983-type table). The EN 1665 table (current heavy series) differs for several sizes (e.g. M10 s=16,k=10.4; M12 s=18,k=11.8 per the German reseller table) and has no 3 independent sources found, so it is NOT published. ISO 4162 (small series, s=7,8,10,13,15,18,21) is also a different table (only AFT + stainlessfix found). Several 'DIN 6921' pages online (Vidasan, itafasteners.com, Aspen PDF, engineeringhardware.com) actually show the flange NUT DIN 6923 table (s=8..30) or look auto-generated -- ignore them. Do not mix DIN 6921 s (M12=16) with EN 1665 s (M12=18). Coarse pitch only; M5-M20.

verification.checks_done: Re-fetched live (HTTP 200) fuller, hjf, qewit, degademir, aft, capitalbolts, kova, theo and parsed every table myself (python/tbl.py). Matrix 8 rows x 10 value columns (P,b,c,dc,ds_min,e,k,k1,s_max,s_min) x 8 parsed sources: zero numeric disagreements except theo M5 dc 11,58 (vs 11.8). Fuller/hjf/qewit identical in all 26 columns (no CHINESE DIFF) -> one cluster. Additionally fetched fasteners.eu + boltport DIN-6921 pages live: both are the DIN 6923 NUT table (da,dc,dw,e,h,m,m',s=8..30) -> row semantics of the record (b, ds, k1 columns = bolt) confirmed not nut; no nut value (dc M8 17.9, e M8 14.38, s M12 18) leaked into the record. Found fastenerdata DIN 6921 page (extra cluster) and compared k,dc,e,s,b for 8 rows. Cluster counts per column: P 3 (CH,DG,CAP; M5 only CH,DG=2); b 4 (M5: CH,DG,AFT; AFT has no L-range label); c 2 (CH,DG) FAIL; dc 5 (M5: CH,DG,AFT vs GER+FD 11.58); ds_min 3 (CH,DG,AFT; M20 only CH,DG=2 because capital/kova ds labels are swapped); e 4; k 5-6; k1 2 FAIL; s_max 5-6; s_min 3 (CH,AFT,CAP; M5 CH,AFT=2 and M20 CH,CAP=2).
problems: STRICT clustering: fuller/hjfasteners/qewit are one cluster -> c_min and k1_min have only 2 clusters (Chinese + degademir) -> dropped

M5 row fails: P (only CH+DG = 2 clusters; capital/kova start at M6), s_min (CH+AFT = 2), and dc_max is contested (3 clusters say 11.8 but theo cluster AND fastenerdata say 11.58, k 5.8 on fastenerdata)

Alternative if M5/M20 are wanted: keep them and instead drop columns P, ds_min, s_min (then all kept cells >=3 clusters)

Family label 'EN 1665 · DIN 6921 · ISO 4162 · KS B 1042 · ASME B18.2.1' but the table is DIN 6921 ONLY: theo's EN 1665 table differs (M10 s16 k10.4, M12 s18 k11.8, M16 s24 k15.4), AFT's ISO 4162 table differs (s 7,8,10,13,15,18,21; dc 11.4..32.8); AFT's 'EN1665' page just reprints DIN 6921. Publish as 'DIN 6921' only and do not present it as EN 1665/ISO 4162

Several 'DIN 6921' pages (fasteners.eu, boltport, vidasan, itafasteners, aspen) are really the DIN 6923 flange-nut table (s 8,10,13,15,18,21,24,30; h,m,m' columns); none of their numbers are in the record

fastenerdata (DIN 6921 page) dissents on e_min M10 16.49, M12 17.6, M14 19.76, M16 23.12, M20 28.5 and dc M14 30.0 (4 clusters say 16.5/17.62/19.86/23.15/29.87/30.5); outvoted, kept, but note M12 s=16 here vs 18 in nut/EN 1665 tables
b is only labelled 'L<=125' by CH/DG/capital; AFT 'Thread Length (LT) Basic' has no L range
dc_max/s_max: only CH and AFT print an explicit 'max' header; DG/capital/theo print a bare symbol (same numbers)
ds_min: capital/kova page has Min/Max swapped (Min 6 / Max 5.82) -> excluded; intafast PDF and lawson/hammer product pages agree but are corroboration only
